title: The two-fifths admissibility obstruction for scaling-sharp Strichartz estimates of Dirichlet waves on the two-dimensional Friedlander convex model
source_title: New counterexamples to Strichartz estimates for the wave equation on a $2$D model convex domain
author: Oana Ivanovici; Gilles Lebeau; Fabrice Planchon
difficulty_reason: The cited dispersive parametrix does not itself produce the stronger necessary Strichartz exponent condition. The author constructs a localized family of initial data, isolates the accumulated reflected-wave contribution through the Airy-Poisson phase analysis, and compares the exact initial L2 norm with its spacetime Lr concentration. Optimizing the printed three scales gives the new two-fifths obstruction, with the supporting Airy and orthogonality proofs retained.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem1 only on the exact two-dimensional Friedlander half-space metric, Dirichlet boundary, scaling exponent beta=2(1/2−1/r)−1/q and the localized estimate2. Necessary condition is1/q≤(2/5)(1/2−1/r), including q≥5 when r=infinity; no positive estimate, endpoint sufficiency or generic convex-domain claim. Entire new initial-data construction, reflected-wave isolation, complex-phase remainder proof and parameter optimization read. Classical Airy spectral theory, Poisson summation and real/complex stationary phase are explicit existing prerequisites. Full Appendix spectral normalization retained. Remark3.5 cutoff says chi vanishes where preceding3.4 explicitly discards1−chi. Lemma4 final cardinality power of lambda is mistyped relative to its explicit derivative criterion; selected construction uses the stated uniform N=O(h^−1/3) cutoff and fully supplied nonstationary-phase derivative construction.
